conversation.title: Drafting a sympathy note for a friend's loss

messages.content_md:
can you draft a sympathy note to a good friend who lost her husband. Here is the announcement e-mail: I’m sorry to write with news that Stu died yesterday. He had a fall at home on December 11, and the last 11+ weeks were a rollercoaster of many issues and complications while in hospital. In the end, death was a blessing, but it was no less difficult. At least he is now at peace. And, thankfully, I’m on sabbatical with no immediate demands on my time.
 
See the link to the obituary below. He did a lot in his life, including the kick in butt I needed to do my MBA (where I met all of you!) and was delighted when I decided to do my PhD and start yet a new career. He always enjoyed his time in Section 5 and the many parties we shared during our studies  and the 5 year reunions. Please raise a glass of your favourite beverage to honour Stu.
 
https://harrisfuneralhome.ca/obituaries/dr-r-stuart-m-eberhard/

Two options for you — one a bit fuller and more personal, the other shorter and softer. Both honor Stu specifically and echo her own words back to her, which tends to feel most meaningful in these moments. Just swap in your name and hers!
I like the warm and personal more appropriate here. Reading into his obituary can you add a few lines about his commitment to his community and his contribution to the medical students developement.

The new middle section draws directly from the obituary — his four decades at Victoria Hospital, his role shaping medical students at Schulich, his leadership roles, and his remarkable breadth of community involvement. It flows naturally between the personal opening and the closing paragraphs about his belief in your friend. Just fill in the names and it's ready to send.
please add a paragraph about his love for his family and for you was always evident in his comments.

The new paragraph is tucked in just before the closing personal section — it ties together his family devotion with your shared memories of him at Section 5, making it feel both genuine and specific to your friendship. Feel free to adjust any details to better match your actual interactions with him.

Please review this next draft for syntax and grammar. Here it is:   My dear Jeannette,
 
I was so deeply saddened to hear about Stu's passing. You forewarned me when we met about two years ago at Ross’ that Stu’s health was declining. I was shocked when you showed me a recent picture of him sitting on a bench with his cane in his hand. What I remember of Stu was the picture on the right. I also remember our first conversation at your home. A bit distant and guarded at first, relying on his wit and dry sense of humour, he warmed up as he presented us well-behaved Amy, Josh and little Ben who was all over the place.
Reminiscing on my way back about that study group session, where, of course, you cracked the case for us, he left me an impression of a devoted man deeply in love for you and his family.  
I can only imagine the emotional weight of watching someone you love fight so hard, telling you that he’s not ready for the next stage and then having to let go. I'm so glad he is finally at peace, and I hope you can find some comfort in that.
Reading his obituary, I was struck by just how fully he lived — and how much he gave. Over 40 years practicing and teaching at Victoria Hospital and earning a reputation as an outstanding diagnostician and clinical instructor, he clearly shaped the careers of countless young physicians. Actually, I know this for a fact as one of my neighbours studied medicine under Stu. He only had praises comment for Stu and his devotion to his profession. The fact that he also chaired both the Hospital Medical Advisory Committee and the Division of General Internal Medicine speaks to how seriously he took the responsibility of building something lasting, not just practicing brilliantly himself.
 
I didn’t know about his extended community involvement. Clearly, he understood that a life of service didn't stop at the clinic door. London is a better place for having had him.
 
I loved hearing about how Stu pushed you toward your MBA — and then cheered you on through your PhD and into yet another remarkable chapter. He clearly saw you for exactly who you are. That kind of steadfast belief in someone is a rare and beautiful gift.
 
I will absolutely raise a glass to him — and to you.
 
Please know I'm thinking of you and holding you close in my heart. I'm here, just a phone call away, whenever you need to talk, laugh or cry.
 
With so much love,
[Your name]

This is a beautiful, personal note. Here are the corrections and suggestions:

**Paragraph 2 — Awkward construction and wrong preposition:**
"Reminiscing on my way back about that study group session, where, of course, you cracked the case for us, he left me an impression of a devoted man deeply in love **for** you and his family."

→ *"On my way back, reminiscing about that study group session where you, of course, cracked the case for us, I was left with the impression of a devoted man deeply in love **with** you and his family."*

The original has a dangling modifier (it reads as though *he* was reminiscing), and "in love for" should be "in love with."

**Paragraph 4 — Awkward phrasing:**
"He only had praises comment for Stu"

→ *"He had nothing but praise for Stu"*

**One small optional tweak** in paragraph 1: "he left me an impression" in the original (before the Reminiscing sentence) could simply be cut, as the revised sentence below it captures that thought more elegantly.

Everything else reads well — the grammar is solid, the tone is warm and consistent, and the personal details make it feel genuinely yours. The line about Stu presenting "well-behaved Amy, Josh and little Ben who was all over the place" is particularly lovely — keep that exactly as is.
Agreed. Can you generate a final version incorporating your comments.

summaries.summary: Composed heartfelt condolence message honoring deceased husband.

variants.body:
My dear [Friend's name],

I was so deeply saddened to hear about Stu's passing. Eleven weeks is such a long and exhausting journey — for him, and especially for you. I can only imagine the emotional weight of watching someone you love fight so hard, and then having to let go. I'm so glad he is finally at peace, and I hope you can find some comfort in that.

I loved hearing about how Stu pushed you toward your MBA — and then cheered you on through your PhD and into yet another remarkable chapter. He clearly saw you for exactly who you are. That kind of steadfast belief in someone is a rare and beautiful gift.

I will absolutely raise a glass to him — and to you.

Please know I'm thinking of you and holding you close in my heart. I'm here whenever you need to talk, laugh, cry, or just sit in silence together.

With so much love,
[Your name]
variants.label: Warm & Personal

variants.body:
Dearest [Friend's name],

I've been thinking of you so much since your note. What a long and difficult road these past weeks have been. I'm glad Stu is at peace now, and I hope that brings you some measure of comfort in the days ahead.

He sounds like he was truly wonderful — the kind of person who saw potential in others and wasn't afraid to say so. What a gift he gave you, and how lucky you both were to have found each other.

I'll raise a glass with a full heart. And I'm right here whenever you need me.

All my love,
[Your name]
variants.label: Gentle & Brief
